application_type_full: Tree works: Trees in conservation areas/subject to TPOs
description: This submission is supported by a detailed Arboricultural Appraisal Report dated 10th February 2026 and a Chartered Surveyor?s Defect Analysis Report referenced SR160998. Together, these independent professional reports provide clear arboricultural, structural and safety evidence confirming that removal of the tree is justified, proportionate and necessary in the circumstances.In terms of public amenity, the tree makes only a negligible contribution. It is largely screened from public view and only a small section of the lower stem can be glimpsed from the highway. The canopy itself is not meaningfully visible from public vantage points and does not form a prominent or defining feature within the wider street scene.The tree has been subject to cyclical heavy pruning in the past and now shows limited regenerative response. It is affected by horse chestnut leaf miner and is in a state of declining vitality. Its physiological condition is poor and its long term prospects are limited.While it would be possible to continue managing the tree, retention would not resolve the fundamental issues. The ongoing structural conflict with the boundary wall would remain, as would the pressure from the expanding root plate. The associated liability exposure would continue and the tree would remain fundamentally unsuited to its confined position so close to built structures. In short, further management would only prolong a situation that is structurally unsustainable.To ensure there is no loss of long term canopy cover or amenity, two replacement trees are proposed. These are one Ginkgo biloba and one Liriodendron tulipifera, both 10 to 12 centimetre Select Standards. The new trees will be positioned at an appropriate distance from boundary structures to avoid future conflict. They will be planted in accordance with BS 8545 and provided with proper aftercare and establishment watering to ensure successful long term growth.The proposal aligns with Section 197 of the Town and Cou
